correctness.rationale: Every zero-sum vector has an exact radial plus (q-1)-fold fluctuation decomposition, verified by independent exact rational summation. Strict subadditivity controls fluctuations for all 0<p<2. The radial determinant factors, F is strictly decreasing in p for q>=3 and has one root in (1,p_A). The affine-in-q comparison to q_A proves the other factor G positive whenever F>=0, excluding an earlier obstruction. Critical null vector, dimensions, non-strictness, exclusion of p above endpoint by Li--Weston, and inverse-q asymptotics are explicitly proved. The q=2 path is handled separately. Finite numerical tests are corroboration, not infinite proof.

value.rationale: The once-subdivided equal-arm star is the smallest rooted spherically symmetric family beyond a one-edge star. The exact maximal negative-type exponent, endpoint Euclidean dimension jump, strict subdivision penalty, and sharp inverse-branching asymptotic are natural structural metric-embedding invariants for a full infinite family. The finding is not merely a restatement of star theory or a routine standalone table computation; the two competing spectral sectors require a global first-root proof.
